A black hole is a region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape past its boundary, the event horizon. Most form when massive stars collapse, and giant ones sit at galaxy centres. We detect them by their effects, and in 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of one, in the galaxy M87 [1][2].

Sources:
[1] https://www.nsf.gov/news/media-toolkits/event-horizon-telescope — Event Horizon Telescope (NSF)
